text.p: Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani said on Tuesday he was opposed to changing the constitution to allow his re-election, the official news agency IRNA reported.
It quoted Rafsanjani as telling a gathering of prayer leaders that changing the constitution in order to extend his term in office was not to Iran's benefit.
Rafsanjani's second term ends in July 1997. The constitution bars three consecutive terms.
"People should be sure that as long as I am alive, I will strive and work for the promotion of Islam and the Islamic revolution and they should have not the slighest doubt over this issue," he said.
He said as part of his "determination and endeavor to help solve the problems of the country" he would even accept the post of governor general of any Iranian province.
A leading Iranian parliamentarian had in August called for the removal of legal barriers blocking the re-election of Rafsanjani, a view reiterated by some of the Iranian media.
